title: Daily Dialogue: Teach Him to Ask Before He Commands
summary: Between the ages of 4-6, the child begins to develop the Theory of Mind—he understands that others have thoughts and feelings different from his own. This is a golden window to teach him: how to ask? How to listen? How to recount what happened? The lesson cites his saying ﷺ: «Among the best of you are those best in character» (Sahih al-Bukhari 3559), and the concept of rifq (gentleness) in questioning. The parent who opens dialogue with his child teaches him that asking is more powerful than commanding, and that «a good word is charity» (Sahih al-Bukhari 2989). The lesson offers 5 daily questions with which the parent can initiate dialogue before sleep, all tied to qudwah (exemplary conduct).
try_this: This week: Every night before sleep, ask your child 3 questions from this list: (1) What was the most beautiful thing that happened today? (2) When did you feel happiness? (3) When did you feel sadness, and why? (4) What did you do when you wanted to cry? (5) If you could change one thing about today, what would it be?
reflection_prompts: Have you noticed your child beginning to ask you similar questions during the day?
Which question elicited the deepest response from your child?
